name: Finn Heller
episode: The worker who couldn't read the joke
life: “I still remember hiring a young man whose father once employed me.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Finn by a small Wednesday habit. Finn prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I have hired the same crew for decades. This is the first time two of them have asked to meet me privately.
appearance: Finn is easy to recognize by a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Finn grins on one side while the eyes stay serious when listening.
personality: Finn carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To offer individual conversations before the staff meeting.
family: Peyton Myers is Finn’s cousin. Finn saves a place. Peyton chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A house divided kindly*, Peyton says, “I offered the first shared meal. Both families brought their own salt, which suggests a useful arrangement for the gate.”
connections: Bianca Breen. The break-room manager and staffing contractor agree on a private way to hear individual workers.

reactions.situation: A manager wants the photographed worker to address the crew
reactions.response: Finn offers the pictured worker a private conversation before any meeting with the crew.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Finn starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Finn offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
